headline: Approved terminating the Wharfing Agreement and the Harbor Usage Fee Agreement with Crowley, doing business as Salem Wind Terminal, LLC.
summary: Members voted unanimously to terminate two agreements with Crowley, doing business as Salem Wind Terminal, LLC: the Wharfing Agreement and the Harbor Usage Fee Agreement. Staff said new or shorter-term agreements, or a Port Authority regulation, may follow. The meeting also discussed parking lot changes, including the Passport parking app and the $1.25/HR rate, but no vote was taken on them.
decisions: Approved terminating the existing Wharfing Agreement with Crowley doing business as Salem Wind Terminal, LLC, unanimously.
Approved terminating the existing Harbor Usage Fee Agreement among the Salem Harbor Port Authority, the City of Salem, and Salem Wind Terminal, LLC, unanimously.
Approved the minutes for the September 3rd meeting, unanimously.

decision_evidence.quote: Mr. Pelletier motioned, seconded by Councilor Turowski, to terminate the existing Wharfing Agreement with Crowley doing business as Salem Wind Terminal, LLC. The motion passed unanimously.

Councilor Turowski motioned, seconded by Mr. Pelletier, to terminate the existing Harbor Usage Fee Agreement between the Salem Harbor Port Authority, the City of Salem, and the Salem Wind Terminal, LLC. The motion passed unanimously.
Mr. Pelletier motioned, seconded by Councilor Turowski, to approve the minutes for the September 3rd meeting. The motion passed unanimously.

decision_titles: Termination of Wharfing Agreement with Crowley (Salem Wind Terminal, LLC)
Termination of Harbor Usage Fee Agreement with Salem Wind Terminal, LLC
plain_text:
SALEM HARBOR PORT AUTHORITY
98 WASHINGTON STREET, SALEM, MASSACHUSETTS  01970 
(978) 619-5685 PLANNING 
(978) 741-0098 HARBORMASTER 
 
MEETING MINUTES: October 15, 2026 
A
 public meeting of the Salem Harbor Port Authority was convened at 5:00 pm via Zoom web 
conference.  
M
embers present: Councilor Turowski, Capt. Ryan, and Philip Pelletier 
Others Present: Capt. Bill McHugh – Harbormaster, Daniel Collins – Planning Department 
C
all to Order 
Capt
. Ryan called the meeting to order at 5:00pm. Roll was called. 
Po
rt Updates 
• Wharfing Rights Agreement
o Capt. McHugh reported that there was a Wharfing Rights Agreement in place starting in 2014
through COVID, then the agreement was renegotiated with Crowley. He said Crowley’s role has
c
hanged, that they are no longer going to be the long-term lease holder on the property and it is
undecided whether they will operate the terminal due to the pullback of federal funding.
Crowley will remain as project manager.
o The Wharfing Agreement with Crowley needs to be terminated and reassigned to another
entity, the Massachusetts Clean Energy Center.
o Capt. McHugh envisions there may need to be shorter term agreements for the time being.
M
r. Pelletier motioned, seconded by Councilor Turowski, to terminate the existing Wharfing 
Agreement with Crowley doing business as Salem Wind Terminal, LLC. The motion passed 
unanimously.   
• Ha
rbor Usage Fee Agreement
o This agreement allows the City to capture revenues pursuant to deep water vessel arrivals. This
r
evenue helps fund services that ensure safe passage of vessels in the harbor.
o This was originally set up as a tariff system, but the City is not operating the berth directly.
o The agreement was in place between the City and Crowley. It was not intended to be used
during the construction phase for support vessels.
o Capt. McHugh said they are looking to have this agreement terminated and they will renegotiate
a new agreement or create a Port Authority regulation. Mr. Collins said a new agreement would
be
 substantially similar.
o A company does not need to be in place for the agreement, but if there ends up being one
t
erminal operator then it may make sense
DRAFT
Councilor Turowski motioned, seconded by Mr. Pelletier, to terminate the existing Harbor Usage Fee 
Agreement between the Salem Harbor Port Authority, the City of Salem, and the Salem Wind 
Terminal, LLC. The motion passed unanimously. 
 
 
Staff/Authority Updates  
• Mr. Collins reported that there are no 2027 meeting date conflicts with non-Christian holidays. He 
said the only conflict date is New Years Day so at the December meeting, he will look to reschedule 
or cancel the meeting.  
• Mr. Collins will circulate the 2027 meeting schedule soon.  
• Capt. McHugh provided an update on the parking changes. The parking lot is intended to support 
marine use, but over recent years has been used for non-marine use parking.  
• Capt. McHugh said they are trying to create turnover in the lot.  
• The Passport Parking App has been adopted.  
• Current parking is $1.25/HR with residents receiving a discount. 
• All Passport signage went up in early September with an intended start date of October 1st.  
• Capt. McHugh said the lot is now being used as intended. Roughly 25 MBTA commuters use the lot 
every day. Only one or two commuters have been lost with the parking fee.  
• Commercial uses are not seeing an impact.  
• They are still seeing residents giving out visitor passes, but they are being given warnings followed 
by citations.  
• Capt. McHugh said the intent is not to create revenue but is intended to support marine industrial 
use.  
• He said it may make sense to consider opening a Passport session before the lot opens, or to offer 
one-day discount codes for users to be distributed by excursion operations and ferry operators. 
• Capt. McHugh said that based on the data, he thinks lot usage is heading in the right direction but 
wants to continue to review.  
• He said it is important to continue to educate residents about the parking lot payment system.  
• The City receives resident information from license plate registrations through the RMV and if 
residents on not the list, they should reach out to the City.  
• Councilor Turowski said the staff at the ferry terminal have been very helpful to residents.  
• Councilor Turowski said residents have noted that the lot appears to be underutilized.  
• Capt. McHugh said he thinks the peak utilization they’ve seen so far is between 65-75% on a 
Saturday in October. He expects it will be much higher in the summertime.  
• Councilor Turowski asked if they could consider weekday versus weekend rates in the future. Capt. 
McHugh said that could be difficult for tourists or vacation-time. He said they could look at it in the 
future. He does not think the $1.25/HR is exorbitant. He said it will be important to look at the data.  
 
Harbor Master Report 
• Capt. McHugh said they will start using the large ferry this weekend to increase capacity as they 
move towards Halloween. The Hingham run will start this weekend.  
 
Public Comment 
• Peg Harrington, an abutter and resident of Derby Street neighborhood, expressed frustration about 
having to register visitor’s license with the City or the Passport app for the ferry lot. She is frustrated 
that there are three different models for parking in the City. She said she finds the signage 
confusing.  
DRAFT
• Wendy Walsh noted that she sent an email with ideas for improvement for segmenting the lot for 
residents. She noted that people have issues finding neighborhood parking. She said October is very 
difficult for residents. She said any price is a deterrence for residents. 
 
Approval of the Minutes 
Mr. Pelletier motioned, seconded by Councilor Turowski, to approve the minutes for the September 3rd 
meeting. The motion passed unanimously.   
 
Adjournment 
Mr. Pelletier motioned, seconded by Capt. Ryan, to adjourn. The motion passed unanimously.
